blocks.text: TWO KINGDOMS
Zedekiah. A prophet among the captives in Babylon, named in Jeremiah's letter with Ahab son of Kolaiah.
SCRIPTURE SAYS
Prophesied “a lie unto you in my name” (Jeremiah 29:21)
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Nebuchadnezzar · Zedekiah
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW HE SPOKE

He was one of the prophets among the captives: the letter answers those who said “The LORD hath raised us up prophets in Babylon”, and warns, “Let not your prophets and your diviners, that be in the midst of you, deceive you”.

HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
Foretold: the king of Babylon would slay him before the captives' eyes. Jeremiah 29:21–22
TRADITION SAYS

A learned Hebrew told Origen that the two elders in the story of Susanna were the men of Jeremiah 29: “The Lord make you like Zedekias and Achiab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire”. Another Hebrew told him they had deceived the captives' wives by claiming to explain “the things concerning Christ”. Jeremiah 29:21–23 Susanna 1:5 [44] Who says so: Origen, Letter to Africanus 7–8, reporting what Jewish teachers told him, first half of the 3rd century AD
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
Jeremiah 29
PASSAGES · 3
Jeremiah 29:8–9 Jeremiah 29:15 Jeremiah 29:20–23
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture records nothing else about him: no words of his own, no deeds, no date of death.
The text does not say what lie he prophesied; the letter's surrounding words concern the length of the captivity (Jer 29:8–10, 29:28), but they are not attributed to him.
The phrase “roasted in the fire” is part of the curse foretold in Jeremiah 29:22; no narrative of the event exists in Scripture.
